context: Decide the seam before writing the adoption, not during. The shape that satisfies both rules: the RunRequest carries the profile NAME, and the core run service resolves connection policy through a surface-supplied resolver it invokes at adapter-construction time -- MCP passes one that reads BENCHBOX_MCP_CLICKHOUSE_PROFILES, CLI passes one that resolves from its own config or refuses. Policy stays surface-scoped; the execution path is shared; resolution stays late. Reject the two easy answers explicitly: materializing port/secure into the RunRequest at admission (breaks durable withdrawal), and moving the env registry into core (moves MCP policy below the boundary). Before deleting _prepare_adapter_platform_options, port test_clickhouse_profile_withdrawn_by_the_operator_fails_closed to the new call site FIRST and confirm it still fails when resolution is hoisted to admission -- if the ported test passes under a hoisted implementation, it is no longer testing the property.
description:
one-engine-mcp-run-service-adoption's rung 1 requires `_prepare_adapter_platform_options` to be gone from benchbox/mcp/tools/benchmark.py, and its anti-patterns say option translation belongs below both surfaces while security policy stays at the MCP layer. Those two rules collide on one line of that function, and the collision is security-relevant.

_prepare_adapter_platform_options is not purely translation. For ClickHouse it calls resolve_clickhouse_connection_profile(name) -> {'port', 'secure'}, reading the operator-owned BENCHBOX_MCP_CLICKHOUSE_PROFILES registry. It does that deliberately at EXECUTION time, not admission, so that only the profile NAME is ever persisted in a durable job and a queued retry re-resolves against current policy -- withdrawing a profile fails closed for work already in the queue. That is the documented contract in docs/operations/mcp-remote-security.md (the 'Server-owned ClickHouse connection profiles' section).

Neither adoption rule resolves where it goes:
  - Push it below the surface with the rest of the translation, and an MCP-scoped security registry moves into core, contradicting 'keep security admission at the MCP layer' -- and CLI callers inherit an env-var registry that was never meant for them.
  - Keep it at MCP as a pre-filter, and the port/secure tuple is materialized at admission, which is exactly what the current design refuses: the resolved destination would then be persisted in the durable job and replayed after the operator withdrew the profile.

ASYMMETRIC TEST COVER, which is the real risk. The persistence half is pinned by tests/integration/mcp/test_durable_jobs.py:196, which asserts persisted.request['platform_options'] == {'connection_profile': 'reviewed'} -- a rewrite that materializes the port at admission breaks that test loudly. The execution-time re-resolution half is pinned by tests/unit/mcp/test_benchmark_tools.py:364 test_clickhouse_profile_withdrawn_by_the_operator_fails_closed, which drives _prepare_adapter_platform_options directly -- the very function rung 1 mandates deleting. Whoever does the adoption must rewrite that test, and a rewrite that targets the new call site without preserving WHEN resolution happens loses the guarantee silently.

Raised 2026-08-04 from the mcp-v2-platform-options side (#1510 built this boundary) after the one-engine coordination brief.

preserves.behavior: A profile withdrawn by the operator fails closed for work already queued, not just for new admissions
Durable jobs persist only the profile name; the resolved port/secure tuple is never written to job storage
benchbox.mcp still never imports benchbox.cli, and the profile registry stays MCP-scoped rather than becoming a core concern

verifications.description: Only the profile name is persisted in a durable job
verifications.expected: exits 0 both before and after adoption; a failure here means the destination was materialized at admission

verifications.command: PYTHONPATH=. uv run -- pytest tests/unit/mcp -q -n 0 -k withdrawn
verifications.description: A withdrawn profile still fails closed on replay after the translator moves
verifications.expected: exits 0, and the test must still fail if resolution is hoisted to admission -- verify that by hoisting it temporarily, not by reading the test
